name: Mirage (Cactus Compute)
purpose: A small vision model for phones, wearables and robots: describes scenes, detects objects, reads text, makes masks, finds relations and fills structured forms in one pass (vendor blog).

license.name: Apache-2.0 (card tag)
license.notes: Card tag apache-2.0; no LICENSE file in the repo.

architecture.kind: conv-stem encoder (512 px, 16x16 grid, 16 body blocks plus 12 GQA attention blocks, 4 register tokens) with detection and mask heads, a CTC text reader and an 8-layer decoder emitting structured JSON
architecture.why_this_design: blog: a shared encoder feeds boxes, masks and OCR so the decoder generates fewer tokens; Hadamard transforms around banded convolutions keep channel mixing small (8x fewer weights than a full matrix)

variants.notes: about 22 MB at 2 bit per the blog; the repo file mirage.safetensors is 0.22 GB; runs through the cactus package

pc-12gb.notes: 0.25 GB against a VRAM budget of 9.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-16gb.notes: 0.25 GB against a VRAM budget of 13.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-24gb.notes: 0.25 GB against a VRAM budget of 21.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-32gb.notes: 0.25 GB against a VRAM budget of 29.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

mac-16-24gb.notes: 0.25 GB against a GPU share of about 12 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-32gb.notes: 0.25 GB against a GPU share of about 22 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-64gb+.notes: 0.25 GB against a GPU share of about 52 GB (KV cache not included)

other: cactus-compute Python package and Cactus engine (Needle, Whistle, Mirage share binaries)

benchmarks.name: latency on Samsung Galaxy S26, end to end
VQAv2 consensus credit with Qwen3-0.6B reading Mirage's JSON (256 questions)
benchmarks.variant: another image's record gives 22.2; no trace 33.1

strengths: 51M parameters: scene graph, boxes, masks and text in about 100 ms on a phone
weaknesses: text reader covers 306 Latin characters only
decoder output may infer details wrongly (generated reasoning trace)
weak on open VQA when paired with a tiny text model (31 of 100)
best_for: on-device camera pipelines, cheap screenshot pre-reading
soft.maturity: tiny vendor release with a browser sandbox; 44k downloads, 470 likes

tona_fit.reason: Small enough to run beside any worker, but its 51M-parameter perception is not a document or code reader; Tona's use for it would be structured screenshot pre-reading, which no source here evidences.
blockers: runs only through the Cactus engine

open_questions: OCR accuracy on screenshots and German text (Latin-1 coverage is stated, accuracy is not)
